dedupe_keys.name: border crossings of the world bcw

description: The Border Crossings of the World (BCW) dataset records international border crossings from 1993 to 2020, where a crossing is an instance of a highway crossing an international border. For each crossing it records features of the road itself, such as single-lane or multi-lane, and the presence or absence of filtering infrastructure for search and inspection, such as official buildings, gates and inspection lanes, coded by visual inspection of publicly available satellite imagery. Coverage is global. It was produced by Michael Kenwick, Beth Simmons and Richard McAlexander and is published on Harvard Dataverse (version 1.1, July 2024) under CC0 1.0, as tabular files (the main dataset, a full version and a coder-level file), an R transformation script, a codebook and a README. Caveats: coding depends on imagery availability and resolution, so infrastructure presence may be missed, and the unit is the highway crossing, not rail or minor roads. The crossings are nodes of international road networks for network flow and capacity planning of cross-border corridors, and for hazard exposure of border facilities. It complements the BTS border crossing entry data for US land ports.
